text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Macedonian parliament to discuss inter-ethnic relations on Wednesday. The constitutional court to discuss the constitutionality of the Law on use of national minorities' languages. Students of the teachers academy invited to participate at the parliament session.

- According to revision in the private savings bank TAT from Bitola, there was double bookkeeping. Around 104 million German marks registered in the bank, but 40 million were not. Government ministers to be investigated whether they had influence in previous revisions which showed good business results for the bank.

- The ministry of internal affairs to investigate illegal imports of medicines whose dates have expired. According to the World Bank, medicines in Macedonia are extremely expensive, sometimes up to 20 times more than prices on world markets.

- UNPREDEP halts withdrawal from observation posts at the Macedonian-Albanian border. Only one of nine observation posts towards Albania closed. UNPREDEP expecting instructions from U.N. Secretary-General after the Macedonian government's letter to the U.N. Security Council explaining reasons why the force should not be withdrawn.

- "The scandal in the private TAT savings bank is the same as the one in Valona, Albania. The government should resign and call early elections," says opposition IMRO-DPMNY party. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
